source.title: Visual Autoregressive Modeling: Scalable Image Generation via Next-Scale Prediction
source.authors: Keyu Tian; Yi Jiang; Zehuan Yuan; Bing-Yue Peng; Liwei Wang

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some figure text is garbled in extraction, but the main scaling equations and findings are stated in the text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling-law behavior for visual image-generation models, extending the claim to another modality.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own scaling sweeps and fitted test-loss curves. Comparisons to other image-generation model families and ablation results are not included as rows because they do not measure scaling-law behavior. Claims about language-model scaling and compute-optimal parameter/token allocation are discussed or cited, not tested here.
record.test_reason: The study trains 12 VAR image-generation transformers (18.5M–2.0B parameters) on ImageNet. It fits power laws of ImageNet-validation test cross-entropy loss against parameter count and Pareto-frontier compute. This is a new setting (visual autoregressive generation) that bears directly on V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that VAR test loss (and token error) follow clear power laws in parameters and optimal training compute, with Pearson coefficients near −0.998. They present this as initial verification of LLM-like scaling laws in visual generation and as a basis for performance prediction. They also state that larger VAR models are more compute-efficient, consistent with Kaplan/Henighan.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a visual autoregressive image-generation model using next-scale prediction and evaluates ImageNet test loss; it does not reproduce language-model pretraining or the original language-model scaling-law setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Token prediction error rate follows power-law fits in N and Cmin, with very small exponents (−0.0067 to −0.016).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In VAR image models, token error rate declines as a shallow power law in parameters and Pareto-frontier compute.

fits_no_version.finding: FID improves monotonically with VAR size: 3.30 (310M), 2.57 (600M), 2.09 (1.0B), 1.92 (2.0B) in Table 1. The authors contrast this with DiT's marginal or negative gains beyond 675M. No fitted law is given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generation quality (FID) of VAR image models improves steadily with parameter count, unlike DiT beyond ~675M.

record.problems: The scaling evidence is specific to one visual model family and ImageNet. The paper reports fitted curves but no out-of-sample extrapolation test; it does not vary the parameter/token allocation to test compute optimality. Uncertainty intervals for the fits are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No scaling-loss results were left out. Token-error fits are included as rows but are not linked to a claim version because they measure error rate rather than cross-entropy loss.

untested.parts: Only image-generation models are studied, not language-model pretraining loss.
The authors claim the laws enable 'performance prediction' but report no out-of-sample test in which small-run fits predict larger runs.
Loss-minimising parameter/token allocation versus compute is not fitted or reported.
Shape is tied to depth by a fixed rule (w=64d, h=d), so depth and width are never varied at fixed parameter count.
Only class-conditional ImageNet image generation with one model family (VAR) is tested. Video, fine-tuning, transfer and controlled repeated-data scaling are not tested.
Zero-shot in-/out-painting and editing are shown only qualitatively, with no scaling relation.
No comparison of fitting methods, parameter counting, schedules or data choices.

record.verdict_notes: The parameter sweep covers only ~2 orders of magnitude; the 6-orders claim refers to Cmin, and Cmin is drawn from training curves via a Pareto frontier. The background section defines L as reducible loss normalised by irreducible loss, but it is unclear whether an irreducible term was subtracted before fitting the reported equations. No fit uncertainties are reported. Training repeats ImageNet for 200–350 epochs, so the laws were obtained under heavy data repetition, but repetition is not varied as a factor. The record's version linking is correct, and R5–R8 are properly left unlinked.

versions.untested_parts: The scaling tests use visual image-generation models, not language models.
The paper fits curves across its sweep but does not report an out-of-sample test in which fits from small runs predict much larger runs.
The study examines loss against parameter count and Pareto-frontier compute, but does not test how the loss-minimising parameter/token allocation changes with compute.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count is reported.
Tests image-generation models trained on ImageNet; does not test video, repeated data, fine-tuning, transfer, or other training regimes.
The paper reports zero-shot image-editing and in-/out-painting examples, but does not test downstream performance as a function of scale or pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitting methods, parameter-counting conventions, data choices, or training schedules for their effect on exponents is reported.

relationships.condition: VAR next-scale-prediction image transformers, 18.5M–2.0B parameters, trained 200–350 epochs on ImageNet, test loss on the 50k-image validation set (last-scale and all-scale average)
relationships.reason: R1–R4 give clean power-law fits of test loss against N (exponents −0.23/−0.20) and Cmin (−0.13/−0.16), with Pearson near −0.998/−0.99; the average-loss fit is said to span 6 orders of magnitude in Cmin.
relationships.display_finding: Last-scale and average test-loss fits had parameter exponents −0.23/−0.20 and compute exponents −0.13/−0.16, with Pearson correlations near −0.998/−0.99 and the average-loss compute fit spanning six orders of magnitude.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
